main_text.p: Irum illum militarem. Possunt & verba alia excidisse. Nec pono tamen ista, sed propono.

Pa.41.l.15. A'νλοκραλέ-ων ἀπoθνησκόντων τὰς εἰκό-νας. Quæ illę sunt? quis me docet? In Nummis, in statuis nihil tale video, nec usquam in cruce propositos Principes defunctos. Subdubitabam an ad aquilas respiceret, quæ volantium habitu, & in cælum tendentium passis aliis conspiciuntur in Nummis, & additum Consecratio. Scilicet quasi Jovis illa ales animam defuncti ferret in gremium Jovis. Certè quidem eam formam crucis esse & Patres monent & res ipsa docet. Sed non placet. Hoc nunc magis, intelligere eum imagines defunctorum Principum, quæ ordine innexæ in militaribus signis.

page.notes: Greek line in the paragraph beginning "Pa.41" is small and partly doubtful; transcribed as best read. The printed Roman numeral and reference "I 5" at the foot of the text is a catchword-like mark and has been treated as part of the text's end, with the page number and running head as printed. The initial I is a woodcut letter joined to "rum" as printed text "I"; the first line "rum illum militarem." continues from the previous page.
